One planet, and every living thing we know of.

Take a slow turn around Earth and see what sets it apart from every other world we’ve found.

Scroll

Seven-tenths of it is ocean

Oceans cover about 71% of the surface and hold roughly 97% of the planet’s water. From space, that’s why it looks blue.

A thin shell of air

The atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Almost all weather happens in the lowest dozen kilometres or so.

4.54 billion years old

Earth formed about 4.54 billion years ago. Life showed up early: the oldest fossils we’ve found are around 3.5 billion years old.

Always moving

Earth circles the Sun at about 29.8 km every second, finishing a lap every 365.25 days while it spins once about every 24 hours.
